Angadi, Advocate For R2) This Miscellaneous First Appeal Is Filed Under Section 173(1) Of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Against The Judgment And Award Dated 04.07.2017 Passed In Mvc No.123/2015 On The File Of The Ii Additional Senior Civil Judge And Member, Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hubballi, Partly Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation And Etc., -2- Nc: 2024:Khc-D:8313-Db Mfa No. 103396 of 2017 This Miscellaneous First Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day, Basavaraja, J., Delivered The Following: Judgment
texts.facts: Appellant/Claimants have preferred this appeal against the judgment and award dated 04th July, 2017 passed in MVC No.123 of 2015 by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hubballi (for short hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal"). 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to with their rank and status before the Tribunal. 3. Brief facts of the case leading to this appeal are that the petitioners filed petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998 seeking compensation of Rs.1,25,00,000/- for death of Vinuth in the accident. It is stated in the claim petition that on 08th July, 2014, Vinuth K M, was proceeding in VRL Volvo bus bearing registration No.KA- 25/D-1400 towards Mumbai from Shivamogga on Bangalore- Pune National Highway and while so performing the journey, on the next day, i.e. on 09th July, 2014 at 5.00 pm, when the bus was moving in the vicinity of Vele village, near Khabatki tunnel, the driver of the bus lost control and drove the same in rash NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB and negligent manner and dashed to the hill and as a result the said Vinuth sustained grievous injuries and succumbed at the spot. It is further stated in the claim petition that as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged 24 years, was hale and healthy and has completed Hospitality Management course from SVGH Vocational Training College and completed a program of training and assessment in Food Safety and Catering and also completed training course in Personal Safety and Social Responsibilities, Fire Prevention and Fire Fighting Personnel Survival Techniques, Elementary First Aid form Sea Scan Maritime Foundation and also completed training course in Passenger-ship Familiarisation Course and Crisis Management Operational Level and also completed HACCP Course programme in Mumbai. The deceased was working as Assistant Waiter in Cruise i.e. MSC Crociere SA through Imperial Ocean Management Private Limited, Mumbai and earning a salary of more than US$ 1,500.00 per month from 15th June 2013 to 04th April, 2014 on contract basis. It is also contended that during the service he even completed a programme of Smt. Shaila W/O Manjappa K.D vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174117064/ 2 training which is approved by the UK Maritime and Coastguard Agency in Security Awareness. The deceased was experienced in the said field as he had worked in P & O Cruises before joining MSC Crociere SA. Further, the deceased after completion of contract NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB period had applied for renewal of contract through the Imperial Ocean Management Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai. Due to sudden demise of the deceased, petitioners are put to mental agony and shock and on all these grounds, preferred the claim petition. 4. After service of notice, respondents appeared through their counsel. Respondent No.2 filed objections. Respondent No.1 has not filed objection. 5. The sum and substance of the statement of objections of respondent No.2 is that the petition is false, frivolous and fabricated not tenable in the eye of law. Further, it is also denied as to the averments made in the claim petition. It is also contended that the deceased Vinuth K M did not travel in the bus on the date of the alleged accident. It is admitted that the respondent No.1 is the owner of the bus and the said bus was insured with the respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident. The respondent no.2 has no knowledge about the relationship between the deceased and the petitioners and the compensation claimed is very exorbitant. It is also contended that the legality, validity and authenticity of the alleged qualification and certified are not from notified and recognised educational institutions and the deceased had no income as on the date of the accident. Further, the driver who was driving the vehicle at the alleged NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB time of accident did not possess, legal, valid and effective driving licence and the owner, knowingly, violated the conditions of the insurance policy. On all these grounds sought to dismiss the claim petition. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues. 6. To prove the case of the petitioners, four witnesses were examined as PWs1 to 4 and forty documents were produced as Exhibits P1 to P40. Respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf, but marked six documents as R1 to R6 with consent. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the appellant/claimants have preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation. 7. During the pendency of the appeal, the appellants have filed application in IA.I of 2014 under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to issue witness summons to the witness shown in the application and also produced the salary certificate of deceased Vinuth who worked at MSC Orchestra Vessel under Panama Flag from 15th June 2013 to 04th April, 2014 as Assistant Waiter. The NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB Respondent No.2-Insurer has filed its written objections to the said application. Now, the claimants have filed application under Order LXI Rule 27 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to adduce additional evidence.
texts.arguments: 8. Smt. Sunanda P. Patil, learned counsel for the appellants would submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side and requires to be enhanced. The Tribunal failed to note that the deceased was aged 24 years as on the date of accident and was hale and healthy. The deceased had completed Hospitality Management Course from SGVH Vocational Training College, Mugtihalli, Chikkamagalur and completed a programme of training and an assessment in Food Smt. Shaila W/O Manjappa K.D vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174117064/ 3 Safety in Catering and also completed training courses in Personal Safety and Social Responsibilities, Fire Prevention and Fire Fighting Personnel Survival Techniques, Elementary First Aid from Sea Scan Maritime Foundation and also completed training course in Passenger-ship Familiarisation Course and Crisis Management Operational Level and also completed HACCP Course Programme from International Cruises Culinary Academy Pvt. Ltd. in Mumbai. It is further submitted that prior to accident, the deceased was working as an Assistant Waiter on contract basis in Cruise, MSC Crociere SA through Imperial Ocean Management Private Limited, Mumbai and earning more than Rs.US$ 1500.00 per month from 15th June, 2013 to 04th April, 2014. The deceased was experienced in the said field as NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB he had worked in P & O Cruises before joining MSC Crociere SA. However, he submits that Tribunal erred in considering the income of the deceased only at Rs.10,000/- per month for awarding compensation towards loss of dependency. Learned Counsel further submitted that the Tribunal has failed to consider the documents Exhibit P23 and 29, so also, has ignored the evidence of PW2 as to the income of the deceased. Further, the Tribunal has also not properly considered the future prospects of the deceased. The Tribunal has observed that the petitioners have not produced documents to show that the deceased was working as on the date of accident. It is stated that due to inadvertence, the appellants have not produced the said evidence before the Tribunal and the proposed additional evidence is very much required to adjudicate the matter in dispute. If this application is not allowed, the appellants would be deprived of getting just and reasonable compensation. On all these grounds sought to allow the application and remand the matter to the Tribunal to lead additional evidence. To substantiate the submissions, the learned counsel relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAJWATI @ RAJJO AND OTHERS NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB v. UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in (2023) ACR 183 (SC) and the decision of this Court in the case of MANAGER, RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. v. SHIVALEELA AND OTHERS reported in 2020 ACJ 2421. 9. Per contra, Sri C.V. Angadi, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 submit that based on the available evidence on record, the Tribunal has awarded just compensation in accordance with law and facts and there is no need for interference. He also submitted that the respondents have satisfied the award and at this belated stage, without assigning any appropriate reasons, the appellants have filed this application. There is no merit in the application and hence, he sought for dismissal of application as well as the main appeal. 17. Learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurer has filed statement of objections contending that the application filed under Order XLI Rule 27 of Code of Civil Procedure seeking issuance of witness summons is neither maintainable in law nor on facts. The courts are duty- bound to award just compensation as observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAMLA v. NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMTED reported in Smt. Shaila W/O Manjappa K.D vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174117064/ 6 2019 ACJ 559. It is also pertinent here to refer to the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAJWATI (supra), wherein at paragraph 19 of the judgment, it observed as under: "19. It is well settled that Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficial piece of legislation and as such, while dealing with compensation cases, once the actual occurrence of the accident has been established, the Tribunal's role would be to award just and fair compensation. As held by this Court in Sunita (Supra) and Kusum Lata (Supra), strict rules of evidence as applicable in a criminal trial, are not applicable in motor accident compensation cases, i.e., to say, "the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases"."
